events.title: Ashurnasirpal II of Assyria
events.description: Ashurnasirpal II rebuilds Assyria's military power and establishes Kalhu (Nimrud) as the new capital with an enormous palace.

events.title: Shalmaneser III and the Battle of Qarqar
events.description: Shalmaneser III of Assyria meets a coalition of western kings at Qarqar (853 BC), including King Ahab of Israel with 2,000 chariots.

events.title: The Black Obelisk
events.description: Shalmaneser III's Black Obelisk depicts King Jehu of Israel kneeling and paying tribute to the Assyrian king—the only known depiction of an Israelite king.

events.title: Carthage is founded
events.description: Phoenicians from Tyre found Carthage in North Africa (modern-day Tunisia), which grows into a dominant naval power in the western Mediterranean.

events.title: The First Olympic Games
events.description: The first Olympic Games are held in Olympia, Greece, in honor of the god Zeus. They are then held every four years for over a thousand years.

events.title: Rome is Founded
events.description: According to tradition, Romulus founds the city of Rome. Archaeological findings confirm settlement on the Palatine Hill from this period.

events.title: Homer's Iliad and Odyssey
events.description: The Greek epics the Iliad and the Odyssey, attributed to Homer, are written down and shape Greek culture and identity for centuries to come.

events.title: Tiglath-Pileser III of Assyria
events.description: Tiglath-Pileser III reforms the Assyrian Empire with a professional standing army and a policy of mass deportation of conquered peoples.

events.title: Assyria Conquers Samaria
events.description: Shalmaneser V and Sargon II of Assyria conquer Samaria, the capital of the Northern Kingdom, and deport the population. The northern Israel ceases to exist as a kingdom.

events.title: Sennacherib and Nineveh
events.description: Sennacherib makes Nineveh his capital and builds an enormous palace. He besieges Jerusalem in 701 BC but fails to capture the city.

events.title: Greek City-States Flourish
events.description: City-states such as Athens, Sparta, Corinth, and Thebes develop different forms of government. Athens begins its path toward democracy.

events.title: Kushite Pharaohs in Egypt
events.description: Nubian kings from Kush conquer Egypt and establish the 25th dynasty. Pharaoh Taharqa is mentioned in the Bible in connection with Sennacherib's campaign.

events.title: The Fall of Nineveh
events.description: Babylonians and Medes destroy Nineveh in 612 BC. The Assyrian Empire collapses completely shortly after. The prophecy of the prophet Nahum is fulfilled.

events.title: The Neo-Babylonian Empire
events.description: Nabopolassar establishes the Neo-Babylonian (Chaldean) empire and frees Babylon from Assyrian control.

events.title: The Battle of Carchemish
events.description: Nebuchadnezzar defeats Egypt and the remnants of Assyria at Carchemish. Babylon takes control over the entire Near East.

events.title: Solon's Reforms in Athens
events.description: Solon implements democratic reforms in Athens: abolition of debt slavery, a new class system, and a legal code that lays the foundation for Athenian democracy.
